headline: OWASP Agentic AI Top 10 formalizes new security risks for autonomous AI (2026)
summary: Agentic AI applications, which take autonomous actions, introduce distinct security challenges. The OWASP Agentic AI Top 10, published in early 2026, formalizes these new risks and defensive patterns.
details: Agentic AI applications, powered by LLMs, autonomously act on external tools and APIs based on model reasoning, not direct user instructions. This rapid shift from research to production has outpaced security practices, leading to a new class of operational failures distinct from non-agentic LLM applications.

Unlike non-agentic LLMs where the user decides on the model's output, agentic systems operationalize model outputs as system actions. This fundamentally changes the security boundary, as the model's output directly affects external systems.

While existing LLM security patterns still apply, the cost of a bypass is significantly higher. A prompt injection in an agent can lead to data exfiltration, record modification, message sending, or code execution, expanding the defensive surface area to include every tool and action the agent can invoke.

The high operational tempo of agentic systems, with potentially tens of tool invocations per minute without human oversight, makes human-review-based mediation impractical. This necessitates a shift towards policy-based mediation, where every tool invocation is checked against predefined rules.

The OWASP Agentic AI Top 10, released in early 2026, identifies ten critical risk categories for agentic AI deployments. These include Tool Misuse (agents using tools unintendedly), Unauthorized Actions (agents taking unrequested actions), and Goal Manipulation (attackers altering an agent's objective).

headline: Get a 27-inch 1440p 240 Hz OLED gaming monitor for $349 at Walmart
summary: The Asus ROG Strix XG27AQDMESZ QD-OLED display is currently 34% off, offering a premium 240Hz gaming experience at an exceptional price for OLED technology.
details: Gamers can now grab the Asus ROG Strix XG27AQDMESZ, a 27-inch 1440p 240 Hz QD-OLED gaming monitor, for just $349 at Walmart. This represents a significant 34% discount from its usual retail price of $529, making premium OLED technology more accessible.

Powered by a 3rd Gen QD-OLED panel, the monitor delivers superior color vibrance compared to WOLED alternatives. Users should note that in high ambient light, black levels may appear purple, and its glossy finish, while enhancing contrast, can show reflections.

A standout feature is the 'Neo Proximity' sensor, designed to combat OLED burn-in by automatically turning off the display when a user steps away. This, combined with ASUS's OLED Care Pro functions, offers robust software-based mitigations.

With an instantaneous 0.03 ms response time, 99% DCI-P3 color coverage, and an average Delta-E of less than 2, the monitor is ideal for competitive gaming, media consumption, and even professional color-accurate work. It balances high performance with affordability.

Connectivity options include one DisplayPort 1.4 and one HDMI 2.1 port, alongside a headphone jack. The display also incorporates anti-flicker features and Extreme Low Motion Blur (ELMB) for a smooth visual experience.
